skill.name: datadata-api
skill.description: Query and manage Datadata datasources through a Python CLI. It supports metadata lookup, read-only SQL execution, result downloads, and ducklake data-space table operations.
skill.summary: Use Datadata APIs and a local CLI to explore datasources, run SQL, export results, and manage ducklake data spaces.
skill.author: datadata-team

security_audit.summary: The skill is Datadata-focused and I found no prompt injection or hidden payloads. Most static alerts are false positives from markdown backticks, Chinese documentation, placeholders, and Datadata resource IDs. Confirmed issues involve authenticated network use, local credential storage, API key exposure in device-flow output, broad default permissions, and local result-file writes.

remediation.issue: Full API keys can appear in CLI output during device authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Never print the full key. Show only a short prefix, save it securely, and return a redacted confirmation.

remediation.issue: Device-flow keys request broad write-capable permissions by default.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege permission sets per workflow, and require explicit confirmation before requesting write scopes.

remediation.issue: Downloaded result files can be written to caller-controlled paths.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize execution IDs, constrain default writes to a dedicated directory, and require confirmation before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The CLI persists reusable credentials in a local config file.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Unix 0600 permissions, add platform-specific ACL guidance, and document how to revoke or rotate saved keys.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Default Device Authorization Scope

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission list is hardcoded and reused for both device-flow entry points. It includes write and replace-file scopes beyond many documented read-only tasks.

content.value_statement: Teams need a safer way to inspect Datadata sources without building custom API calls. This skill provides guided CLI workflows for metadata, SQL execution, exports, and data-space table management.
actual_capabilities: Search public and private Datadata datasources by keyword or username/name.
Fetch datasource metadata, table lists, and table schemas.
Run adhoc SQL with DuckDB or ClickHouse and datasource bindings.
Download execution results as NDJSON or CSV files.
Create, describe, insert into, and drop ducklake data-space tables.
Run Datadata device authorization and store an API key locally.
limitations: Private data and write actions require a Datadata account and API key.
The CLI does not enforce read-only SQL before sending execute-adhoc requests.
Data-space write commands only work with ducklake datasources.
Large result files are saved locally and are not summarized automatically.

use_cases.title: Explore a New Dataset
use_cases.description: Inspect datasource metadata, list tables, and describe selected schemas before writing SQL.

use_cases.title: Build an API Workflow
use_cases.description: Generate a Datadata REST or CLI flow for queries, exports, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Load Data Into a Space
use_cases.description: Create ducklake tables, insert prepared rows, and verify the stored table schema.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Datadata to list tables for datasource <id>. Show table names, schemas, and the next safe step.

prompt_templates.title: Describe One Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Describe table <table> in datasource <id> and explain the columns that matter for a simple query.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Read-Only Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a read-only Datadata SQL query for <question>. Confirm datasource bindings and return the execution ID.

prompt_templates.title: Manage a Data Space
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ducklake data-space table for <dataset>, insert these rows, then describe the table after insertion.

output_examples.output: A numbered list of matching sources with names, owners, visibility, and source type for user confirmation.

output_examples.input: Run a sales summary query and fetch the result.
output_examples.output: The execution ID, saved file path, format, byte count, row count, and suggested preview command.

output_examples.input: Create a products table in my ducklake data space.
output_examples.output: A concise confirmation that the table was created, followed by the next safe insert or describe action.

best_practices: Confirm the selected datasource before running queries or write commands.
Inspect datasource type, tables, and columns before writing SQL.
Keep API keys in environment variables or local config, never in prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not run drop or insert commands without explicit user approval.
Do not load full NDJSON or CSV exports into model context.
Do not send API keys to an unverified base URL or shared command log.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Datadata API key?
faq.answer: Private datasource access, query execution, exports, and write operations require a Datadata API key.

faq.question: Can it search public datasources without login?
faq.answer: Yes. Public datasource search can run without an API key.

faq.question: Can it write data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create, insert into, and drop ducklake data-space tables when the key has write permission.

faq.question: Where are query results stored?
faq.answer: Results are written to a local file, usually under the system temp directory unless an output path is supplied.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I verify before running SQL?
faq.answer: Verify the datasource, table names, column names, query engine, and that the SQL is read-only.
